reuse.why: The change reuses getBulkBudgetCategories, averageToBudget, extractTagsFromText, spreadsheet access, batching, and the existing undoable handler pattern.

duplication.why: Category eligibility and amount sign conversion remain shared across existing actions and the new consumer without duplicating decision logic.

placement.why: Eligibility stays in the budget category selector, action orchestration stays in actions.ts, and method registration stays in app.ts.

scope.why: The edits are confined to the requested bulk budget policies, new action, handler registration, and relevant tests.

maintainability.why: The centralized policy and explicit option are straightforward to maintain, although the selector comment incorrectly says hidden categories are always skipped.

bypasses_abstraction.where: All six month-wide actions use getBulkBudgetCategories, and setLastMonthSpending uses averageToBudget for sign conversion.

disguised_duplication.where: The new exclusions are defined once in getBulkBudgetCategories and consumed directly by every month-wide action.

abstraction_drift.where: getBulkBudgetCategories renames and makes optional its existing hidden-category parameter; the added exclusions are shared policy predicates rather than consumer-specific branches.
